They shall obtain immeasurable merit.
When such a person’s life comes to an end,
throughout the worlds of the ten directions...
They shall be reborn according to their wishes,
and they shall also behold me as well as the future.

[Recorded by] Minami-sun, Shu-sui Tsū-sei-bu Maro. Dedicated on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month of the third year of Tenpyō. This text is a sūtra outside the official canon. It appears in the *Wǔ-zhōu kān-dìng wěi-jīng mù-lù* (Catalogue of Spurious Sūtras Compiled during the Wǔ-zhōu Period); this is likely a different recension. According to the *Nihon reijiki* (Records of Japanese Spiritual Marvels), there were not a few who practiced the Vaipulya Repentance. Now, repentance is one of the four matters and five recollections, and it is an excellent prescription for curing the three poisons. Having now read this sūtra, which takes the methods of repentance as its primary focus, I find nothing that contradicts the meaning of the Dharma.
